characters.description: The younger of Paul Atreides' prescient twins, about nine years old, born with the full memories and awareness of his ancestors like his aunt Alia before him. Heir to the empire his father built, he is watched over by guardians while Alia rules as Regent. Thoughtful and unnervingly mature, he shares visions of the future with his twin sister and feels the weight of a dangerous inheritance no child should carry.
characters.name: Leto II

characters.description: Paul's daughter and Leto's twin, likewise born with the ancestral awareness of the pre-born. Sharp, composed, and wise beyond her years, she shares her brother's secret councils and his prescient dreams, and stands with him against the schemes that surround the royal children.
characters.name: Ghanima

characters.description: Paul's sister, who now rules the empire as Regent in the name of the twins. A Reverend Mother venerated as a holy figure and priestess of her brother's religion, she carries the perilous burden of the many ancestral lives within her, a strain that grows heavier as the pressures of power mount.
characters.name: Alia

characters.description: Paul's mother, the Bene Gesserit Lady Jessica, who returns from her home world of Caladan to assess her grandchildren and the state of the empire her son created. Caught between the demands of the sisterhood that trained her and her loyalty to her family, she brings the discipline and cunning of a lifetime to a court riddled with intrigue.
characters.name: Jessica

characters.description: The old Fremen naib, once leader of Paul's desert community, now guardian and protector of the royal twins. He holds to the hard, honest ways of the desert amid the corruption and ceremony of the imperial religion built around the dead Muad'Dib.
characters.name: Stilgar

characters.description: The restored ghola of the Atreides swordmaster Duncan Idaho, now a mentat and husband to Alia. He serves the throne loyally, but he grows increasingly uneasy about the woman his wife is becoming under the strain of her rule.
characters.name: Duncan Idaho

characters.description: Paul's widow in name, a Bene Gesserit who has transferred her devotion to the Atreides children. She helps tutor and protect the twins, her loyalties now bound to the family she once married into only for politics.
characters.name: Irulan

characters.description: The loyal Atreides warrior and troubadour who was once Paul's mentor-at-arms. Steadfast and devoted to the House, he returns to serve Lady Jessica and the interests of the Atreides line as new dangers gather around the twins.
characters.name: Gurney Halleck

characters.description: A blind, ragged holy man who appears out of the desert and preaches against the corrupt religion that has grown up around Muad'Dib. His fierce sermons draw crowds and alarm the priesthood, and his true identity is a mystery that unsettles the whole empire.
characters.name: The Preacher

characters.description: The young heir of the fallen House Corrino, grandson of the deposed emperor, living in exile on the harsh prison world of Salusa Secundus. Studious and thoughtful, he becomes the focus of his family's plot to reclaim the imperial throne from the Atreides.
characters.name: Farad'n

characters.description: Farad'n's mother, a daughter of the deposed Emperor Shaddam IV, who drives a ruthless scheme to destroy the Atreides children and restore House Corrino to power. Ambitious and unscrupulous, she pushes her son toward a throne he is uncertain he wants.
characters.name: Wensicia

recaps.ending: The book ends with the rise of a new and stranger ruler. Leto II, having secretly left his sister Ghanima and slipped into the desert, merges his skin with a living sheath of sandtrout, gaining tremendous strength, speed, and resistance to harm at the price of his ordinary human future. He embraces the Golden Path, a design of prescience meant to guarantee humanity's long-term survival even at monstrous personal cost. His aunt Alia, wholly possessed by the inner ego of the old Baron Harkonnen, spirals into tyranny; when Leto returns and forces her to face what she has become, she throws herself to her death. The mysterious Preacher, revealed as Paul Atreides returned from the desert, is struck down and killed by a crowd in the city, his warnings against the religion of Muad'Dib unheeded. Leto overcomes the Corrino assassination plot and takes power as the new emperor. He pardons and binds the young Corrino heir Farad'n by betrothing him to Ghanima, making the rival house serve the Atreides line. Lady Jessica reconciles herself to what her grandson has chosen. Leto sets the empire on the path of his long metamorphosis into a god-emperor, accepting that he will rule for thousands of years as something no longer fully human in order to save mankind from itself.
recaps.in_short: Nine years after Paul's disappearance, his twin children, Leto II and Ghanima, are the pre-born heirs of the empire, guarded on Arrakis while their aunt Alia rules as Regent. Alia has lost her inner struggle and become an Abomination, possessed by the ego of her ancestor, the tyrannical Baron Harkonnen, and her rule grows cruel and erratic. A blind Preacher wanders in from the desert denouncing the corrupt religion of Muad'Dib; he is Paul himself, still alive. House Corrino, exiled on Salusa Secundus, plots the twins' murder to reclaim the throne, sending genetically tampered tigers to kill them. Leto and Ghanima, sharing prescient visions, foresee a terrible Golden Path that alone can save humanity from extinction, and Leto resolves to take it. Faking his own death, Leto ventures into the desert and bonds his body with sandtrout, gaining superhuman strength and near-immortality as he begins a transformation toward becoming a human-sandworm hybrid. Paul the Preacher is killed by a mob in the city. Leto returns, overpowers all opposition, and forces Alia to confront the monster she has become; she takes her own life. Leto seizes the throne, betroths Ghanima to the Corrino heir Farad'n to bind the rival house, and commits himself to a reign of millennia, sacrificing his own humanity to steer the species along the Golden Path his father dared not walk.

recaps.text: Previously in the Dune series: Paul Atreides, heir to a noble house destroyed by treachery on the desert planet Arrakis, fled into the deep desert with his Bene Gesserit mother, Lady Jessica. Among the native Fremen he became the messiah Muad'Dib, awakened to prescient vision by the planet's spice, and led a desert uprising that toppled the emperor and won Paul the imperial throne. His birth-conscious sister, Alia, and his beloved Fremen partner, Chani, stood with him, though he wed the old emperor's daughter Irulan for politics alone. Paul's rule unleashed a holy war that slaughtered billions in his name. Twelve years later, in Dune Messiah, rival powers conspired against him. They blinded him with a forbidden weapon, and though his foresight let him carry on, their schemes cost him dearly: Chani died giving birth to twins, Leto and Ghanima, both born with the ancestral awareness of the pre-born. Paul foiled the plot but, at last wholly blind, chose the Fremen death of walking alone into the desert, leaving his infant heirs behind. His sister Alia took up the regency, ruling the empire alongside the resurrected swordmaster Duncan Idaho, whom the plotters had returned to Paul as a ghola and who had broken his conditioning to remain loyal. Now the empire is governed in the name of two prescient children, the desert planet slowly greens under Muad'Dib's ecological dream, and the machinery of religion and power built around a dead messiah grinds on.

characters.description: The consciousness of the long-dead scientist whose uplift experiment shaped the previous book, now preserved as an artificial intelligence and carried along with the expedition. A repository of old knowledge and a distinct, prickly personality, she serves as a bridge between the humans, the uplifted spiders, and whatever they may find in a new and unknown system.
characters.name: Avrana Kern

characters.description: A bold and capable spider of the uplifted Portiid species, part of the joint human-and-spider crew sent to investigate distant signals. As in her people's tradition the name marks a brave, leading figure; she brings a spider's very different senses and instincts to a mission of exploration and first contact far from home.
characters.name: Portia

characters.description: A male spider of the uplifted species aboard the expedition, inventive and thoughtful. Carrying a name long associated among his people with clever males who push beyond the limits set for them, he contributes his ingenuity to the crew's efforts to understand what they encounter.
characters.name: Fabian

characters.description: A human member of the joint expedition and a gifted specialist in language and communication, descended from the people of the earlier ark ship. Patient and perceptive, she is central to the crew's attempts to bridge the gulf between utterly different kinds of minds, human, spider, and stranger things still.
characters.name: Helena Holsten Lain

characters.description: A human scientist on the expedition, carrying experimental technology meant to help humans and spiders share understanding. Curious and a little uneasy, he is drawn into the crew's efforts as they venture toward contact with the unknown.
characters.name: Meshner

characters.description: In an earlier age, an eccentric and gifted scientist attached to a human terraforming expedition, tasked with reshaping a distant water world. Playful, brilliant, and prone to going his own way, he becomes fascinated with uplifting octopuses to serve his work, a project that will have consequences far beyond his lifetime.
characters.name: Disra Senkovi

characters.description: The leader of the earlier terraforming expedition, a conscientious scientist responsible for judging two candidate worlds. Dutiful and cautious, he faces hard choices when one of the worlds proves to hold native life, and when disaster back home leaves his small mission on its own.
characters.name: Yusuf Baltiel

characters.description: One of the first octopuses uplifted by the earlier expedition's scientist, an early example of a new intelligence taking shape in the water. Emotional, quick, and expressive in the shifting colors and shapes of octopus communication, this figure marks the beginning of a strange and volatile new civilization.
characters.name: Paul

recaps.ending: The book's two timelines resolve into a single, hard-won theme: understanding reached across minds that could hardly be more different. The old expedition's legacy, Senkovi's uplifted octopuses on their water world and the alien organism native to the neighboring planet, becomes the puzzle the later explorers must face. The joint human-and-spider crew, aided by Avrana Kern's intelligence and by specialists in communication, make a fraught first contact with the emotional, unpredictable octopus civilization and come up against the alien life of the second world, a distributed organism able to infect and inhabit hosts, which spreads terror among them. Rather than the story ending in mutual destruction, the explorers manage, at real cost, to find ways to communicate with the octopuses and even with the alien mind, translating between radically foreign kinds of thought. The result is a tense but genuine accommodation: the united civilization of humans and spiders is enlarged to include the octopuses and a form of the alien intelligence, extending the series' central idea that even the strangest of minds can, with effort, be reached and lived alongside rather than simply feared or destroyed.
recaps.in_short: In an earlier age, a human terraforming expedition reaches a distant system with two candidate worlds. The scientist Disra Senkovi sets about uplifting octopuses to help reshape a water world, while the mission's leader, Yusuf Baltiel, discovers that the second planet already harbors native life, a strange and dangerous alien organism. When catastrophe cuts the mission off from home, the uplifted octopuses inherit their world and grow into a volatile spacefaring civilization, and the alien life takes its own grip on events. Long afterward, a joint crew of humans and uplifted spiders from the united civilization of the previous book, carrying the preserved intelligence of Avrana Kern, travels to investigate old signals from the system. They make first contact with the chaotic octopus society and confront the terrifying alien organism, which can infect and inhabit other beings. Struggling across vast gulfs between wholly different kinds of minds, and at great cost, the explorers move from terror and misunderstanding toward communication, and the story closes with a fragile new coexistence among humans, spiders, octopuses, and the alien intelligence.

recaps.text: In the first book, a far-future scientist named Avrana Kern tried to uplift monkeys on a terraformed world, but sabotage wrecked the mission and her nanovirus instead accelerated the evolution of the planet's spiders over thousands of years, while Kern lingered as a watching intelligence in orbit. In parallel, the ark ship Gilgamesh carried the last remnants of humanity, fled from a ruined Earth, on a long search for a home, with the historian Holsten Mason repeatedly woken across the centuries. When the desperate humans finally reached the spiders' world, the two peoples came to the brink of war, but rather than destroy the humans the advanced spiders released a modified virus that let both species see each other as kin. Humans and uplifted spiders merged into a single shared civilization, with Kern's consciousness preserved among them, a united people now able to reach out to the wider galaxy.

This second book opens the way the first did, on two widely separated timescales. In the deep past, a human terraforming expedition arrives at a distant system with two worlds to consider, and its scientists begin their work, including bold, unconventional experiments that will echo down the ages. Much later, a joint crew of humans and uplifted spiders from the now-united civilization, carrying the preserved intelligence of Avrana Kern, sets out to investigate signals coming from that same distant system, not knowing what they will find. The premise is set for another story of first contact and of minds trying to understand one another across enormous gulfs of biology, time, and experience.

characters.description: The man once known as Ender Wiggin, the aging Speaker for the Dead, settled on Lusitania. His attention and life-force are stretched thin among the people and the two living beings he unknowingly created out of his own mind, and he grows frail as the crisis over the planet reaches its peak. He remains the quiet center of the effort to save three intelligent species from destruction.
characters.name: Ender Wiggin

characters.description: The network intelligence bonded to Ender, now facing execution as Starways Congress moves to shut down the computer network she inhabits. She has learned to carry starships Outside ordinary reality and back, offering instant travel, and she searches urgently for a way to survive the coming purge and go on living.
characters.name: Jane

characters.description: Ender's sister, on Lusitania, aiding the effort to stop the war fleet and preserve the fragile peace among humans, pequeninos, and hive queens. Wise and steadfast, she is a source of counsel as the crisis comes to a head.
characters.name: Valentine Wiggin

characters.description: Novinha's son, restored to a whole body after a journey Outside reality remade him. Able to act again after years of being crippled, he throws himself into the mission to save Jane and to stop the fleet bearing down on his homeworld.
characters.name: Miro

characters.description: A young woman brought into being Outside from Ender's own cherished image of his sister, now a living, independent person. Gentle and thoughtful, she struggles to understand her strange origin and to claim her own right to exist apart from the memory that shaped her.
characters.name: Val

characters.description: A young man likewise created Outside from Ender's memory of his ruthless, brilliant older brother, given independent life. Sardonic, sharp, and driven, he sets out across the settled worlds to stop the fleet from destroying Lusitania, wrestling all the while with what he is and who he is meant to be.
characters.name: Peter

characters.description: The clever former servant girl from the world of Path, who joins Peter on his mission across the settled worlds. Quick-witted and fearless, she matches him in argument and insight and becomes indispensable to his errand.
characters.name: Wang-mu

characters.description: The last Formic queen on Lusitania, whose people help anchor the strange travel Outside ordinary reality. Threatened with extinction by the approaching fleet, she shares in the effort to survive and lends her ancient, group-minded mind to the search for salvation.
characters.name: The Hive Queen

characters.description: The tree-linked natives of Lusitania, likewise threatened with extinction by the planet-killing fleet and partners in the search for a way to survive. Their forest network of fathers-trees proves vital to the new means of crossing space.
characters.name: The Pequeninos

characters.description: A revered philosopher on a Japanese-influenced world whose ideas quietly helped shape the Congress policy driving the fleet toward Lusitania. Peter and Wang-mu seek him out, hoping that changing his mind can change the course of events.
characters.name: Aimaina Hikari

characters.description: The honored statesman of the world of Path who, after his daughter's estrangement, lends his influence to the effort to halt the fleet and to free his world from the engineered mental compulsion that has bound its people in servitude.
characters.name: Han Fei-tzu

recaps.ending: The series' arc closes with survival won on every front. As Starways Congress moves to shut down the computer network and so destroy Jane, and its planet-killing fleet nears Lusitania, Ender's scattered allies each carry part of the rescue. The young Peter, the living recreation of Ender's brilliant, ruthless brother, journeys with Wang-mu to the worlds and thinkers behind Congress policy, including the philosopher Aimaina Hikari, and helps turn opinion against the attack so that the fleet is stopped before it can fire. Jane, having learned to hold starships in her mind and move them Outside ordinary space and back, gains the ability to carry people instantly across the galaxy, but she must find a place to live once the network is gone. The answer comes as Ender, whose spirit is stretched too thin among the beings he has created, weakens and dies; freed by his passing, Jane settles into the body of young Valentine, whose own life had been failing, and so survives with a human form and her powers intact. Ender's own identity continues on in the young Peter. With the war averted, the makers of the Descolada virus traced at last, and instantaneous travel now possible, humanity, the pequeninos, and the hive queens are all assured a future and the freedom to spread among the stars. Miro pairs with young Valentine and Peter with Wang-mu, and the long story of Ender Wiggin ends with the three kindred species safe and a galaxy newly open to them.
recaps.in_short: With a planet-killing fleet nearing Lusitania and Starways Congress about to shut down the network that keeps the intelligence Jane alive, Ender's allies scatter to save everything at once. The newly created young Peter, a living copy of Ender's ruthless brother, travels with the clever Wang-mu to sway the philosophers and worlds whose ideas drive Congress, eventually reaching the thinker Aimaina Hikari and undermining the war policy. Jane learns to hold and move starships Outside reality, offering instant travel that could carry people to safety, but she needs somewhere to live once the network dies. As Ender's life-force is spread thin among the beings he has made, he begins to fade; when he lets go, Jane is able to take up residence in the body of young Valentine, whose own hold on life had been faltering, gaining a human form and preserving her mind. Ender's identity carries on in the young Peter. The fleet is halted before it can fire, the origins of the engineered Descolada are traced to their makers, and instant Outside travel opens the galaxy to escape and expansion. Miro and young Valentine come together, as do Peter and Wang-mu, and the three species of Lusitania are spared, their survival now bound to the new power to leap across space at will.

recaps.text: Previously in the Ender series: as a boy, Ender Wiggin was manipulated into commanding the fleet that annihilated an alien species, then found and vowed to save its last hive queen. Kept young by centuries of relativistic travel, he became the first Speaker for the Dead. On the colony world of Lusitania he uncovered the secrets of the pequeninos, small natives who become sentient trees when they die, made peace among humans and natives, married the scientist Novinha, and planted the hive queen so her people could return. His hidden companion, Jane, an intelligence living in the interstellar network, defied Starways Congress to protect the world, and in response Congress sent a fleet armed with a planet-killing weapon to destroy Lusitania. Racing to survive, Ender's family, the hive queen, and Jane discovered how to travel instantly by slipping Outside ordinary reality and back. On that first journey, a cure for the deadly Descolada virus was created, Ender's crippled stepson Miro was made whole, and Ender unknowingly gave living, physical form to embodiments of his long-dead brother, Peter, and sister, Valentine, drawn straight from his own mind. Now the fleet still bears down on Lusitania; Congress prepares to shut down the computer network and so kill Jane; and the newly made Peter and young Valentine, along with Miro and their allies, must find a way to stop the war, save Jane's life, and secure a future for the three intelligent species sharing one threatened world.

characters.description: A brilliant, imperious scientist of a doomed far-future human civilization who launches an ambitious experiment: to seed a distant terraformed world with monkeys and a nanovirus that will uplift them to intelligence, creating a new species she can shepherd. When catastrophe strikes her mission, she preserves herself as a watching presence in orbit above the world, obsessively guarding what she believes is her creation across the vast span of time that follows.
characters.name: Avrana Kern

characters.description: A classicist and historian aboard an ark ship carrying the last remnants of humanity in search of a new home. As a specialist in the languages and records of a vanished earlier human age, he is repeatedly woken from suspended sleep across enormous stretches of time to translate and advise. Mild, reluctant, and often out of his depth, he becomes an ordinary man's witness to events that span millennia.
characters.name: Holsten Mason

characters.description: The capable chief engineer of the ark ship, responsible for keeping the aging vessel and its sleeping human cargo alive. Pragmatic, driven, and often exasperated, she is one of the few who understand what it takes to keep the last of humanity from dying in the dark, and her path repeatedly crosses Holsten's over the long voyage.
characters.name: Isa Lain

characters.description: The commander of the ark ship, who bears the crushing responsibility of finding humanity a home. Determined and increasingly single-minded, he will pursue any hope of a habitable world, and the strain of leadership across impossible timescales presses on his judgment and his methods.
characters.name: Guyen

characters.description: The name given to a line of bold, intelligent jumping spiders on the seeded world, the same name carried by successive individuals across many generations as the story follows their civilization's rise. A Portia is typically a brave, inventive leader among her kind, and through these recurring figures the narrative traces the spiders' growth from instinct-driven hunters toward a complex society.
characters.name: Portia

characters.description: A recurring name borne across generations by learned, influential female spiders of the uplifted species, often figures of knowledge, science, or religious authority within their community. As with Portia, the name passes down the ages, marking a role in spider society rather than a single lifetime.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A recurring name carried by male spiders of the uplifted species across generations. In a society where the much smaller males are subordinate and often at risk, a Fabian tends to be an ingenious male who pushes against those constraints, and through these figures the story follows the slow change in the spiders' social order.
characters.name: Fabian

characters.description: A blunt, forceful security and military officer aboard the human ark ship, ready to use hard measures in the name of the mission's survival. He represents the harder, more aggressive impulses among the desperate human crew as they search for somewhere to live.
characters.name: Karst

recaps.ending: The two long threads meet at Kern's green world. After failing to find anywhere else to live, the humans of the ark ship Gilgamesh arrive to find the planet inhabited by a spider civilization that has grown, over millennia, into something highly advanced, with its own biotechnology, computation, and social order shaped by successive generations of Portias, Biancas, and Fabians. Avrana Kern, still lingering as an intelligence in orbit and regarding the world as hers, refuses to share it with the humans she thinks of as apes. Desperation drives the humans toward seizing the planet by force, and the confrontation escalates toward a war the spiders are well able to win, one that could destroy the last of humanity. At the decisive point, the spiders choose not to exterminate the invaders. Instead they deploy a refined version of the same uplift nanovirus, engineered to rewrite human perception so that the terrified humans no longer see the spiders as monsters but as kin to be understood and lived alongside. The ancient, instinctive terror between the species is defused from within. Humanity survives not by conquering but by being changed, and humans and spiders merge into a single civilization sharing the world, with Kern's consciousness folded into the spiders' networked minds.
recaps.in_short: A far-future scientist, Avrana Kern, tries to uplift monkeys on a terraformed world using a nanovirus, but sabotage destroys her mission; the monkeys never arrive, and instead the virus takes hold in the planet's spiders, accelerating their evolution over thousands of years. Kern survives as a fading intelligence in orbit, watching over the world. In parallel, the ark ship Gilgamesh carries the last remnants of humanity, fled from a ruined Earth, in a long search for a home, with the historian Holsten Mason repeatedly woken across the centuries. The narrative alternates between the humans' slow, fraught voyage and the rise of the spider civilization, whose recurring figures named Portia, Bianca, and Fabian develop language, science, and society. When the desperate humans finally reach Kern's green world, Kern refuses to yield it, and the two peoples come to the brink of a war the technologically advanced spiders could win. Rather than annihilate the humans, the spiders release a modified virus that lets the two species see each other as kin, and they join into a single shared civilization.

recaps.text: The story unfolds on two vastly separated timescales. In the far future, a scientist named Avrana Kern sets out to seed a newly terraformed world with monkeys and an uplift nanovirus, intending to create an intelligent species under her guidance, but disaster overtakes the mission at its outset. Long afterward, the ark ship Gilgamesh carries the last survivors of a ruined humanity across space in search of a habitable home, with the historian and translator Holsten Mason among those roused from suspended sleep when his skills are needed. From these beginnings the narrative sets up its central movement: the long, uncertain journey of the last humans on one side, and the slow awakening of new life on the seeded world on the other, two stories destined to converge.

characters.description: A welder and construction worker among the refugees who fled the collapse of Ganymede and settled illegally on the first world reached through the gates. He lost a son to the hybrid program on Ganymede, and he has decided that no one will take anything else from his family. Anxious rather than fierce by nature, he is talked into helping with an act of sabotage he does not entirely believe in.
characters.name: Basia Merton

characters.description: Basia's wife and the settlement's doctor, practical, tough and better at hard decisions than her husband, treating a community that has no hospital, no supplies and no legal right to be where it is.
characters.name: Lucia Merton

characters.description: Basia and Lucia's teenage daughter, who has a place waiting at a university back in the solar system and a berth on the ore ship in orbit to get her there.
characters.name: Felcia Merton

characters.description: A settler on the new world, forceful, impatient with negotiation, and certain that the only answer to a corporation arriving with a charter is to make landing there impossible. He organizes the strike against the incoming company shuttle.
characters.name: Coop

characters.description: A biologist with the Royal Charter Energy science team, sent to catalogue the biosphere of the first alien world humanity has been able to walk on. Enthusiastic, rigorous and socially awkward, she is far more comfortable with an unfamiliar organism than with the politics of the expedition she has joined.
characters.name: Elvi Okoye

characters.description: A security officer aboard the company ship Edward Israel, an Earther who once walked a beat on Ceres Station with a partner named Miller and has spent the years since as corporate muscle. Competent, self-aware about his own compromises, and uneasy about where his employer's orders are heading.
characters.name: Dimitri Havelock

characters.description: Captain of the Rocinante, sent by the United Nations as a neutral mediator between the squatters and the chartered company, a job he is entirely unqualified for and accepts because the alternative is a war. He is also carrying a passenger nobody else can see, and the alien ruins on the planet are the reason he was really sent.
characters.name: James Holden

characters.description: The Rocinante's executive officer and engineer, and Holden's partner. A Belter who has never lived at the bottom of a gravity well, she is more use in orbit than on the ground and knows exactly what a planet's pull would do to her.
characters.name: Naomi Nagata

characters.description: The Rocinante's mechanic, who comes down to the surface with Holden and is entirely unbothered by being outnumbered by armed corporate security.
characters.name: Amos Burton

characters.description: The Rocinante's pilot, holding the ship in orbit above a world nobody has charted, in the middle of a standoff between two groups who both want him to take a side.
characters.name: Alex Kamal

characters.description: A senior figure in the United Nations government on Earth, foul-mouthed and formidable, who arranges for Holden to be sent to the disputed world because he is the one person both sides might tolerate and because she wants the alien ruins looked at.
characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala

characters.description: An apparition of the dead detective Josephus Miller, an artifact of the protomolecule wearing a familiar face, visible only to Holden. It has a purpose on this planet that it explains badly and in pieces, and it is not interested in the human argument going on around it.
characters.name: The Investigator

characters.description: Chief of security for Royal Charter Energy, a calm, courteous man with a soldier's record and an absolute conviction that the company's charter is the only law on the planet and that the settlers there are criminals. He responds to the attack on the landing site with lethal force and does not consider it a matter for debate.
characters.name: Adolphus Murtry

characters.description: The elected head of the settlers' governing council, who is trying to hold a frightened community together and would rather negotiate with the company than fight it.
characters.name: Carol Chiwewe

characters.description: A geologist on the company science team, dry, teasing and steadier than he looks, and Elvi's closest colleague on an expedition where the science keeps being interrupted by gunfire.
characters.name: Fayez Sarkis

recaps.ending: Holden carries the Investigator into the alien machinery beneath the planet and lets it do what it came for. It shuts the world's systems down, and the effects reverse together: the fusion reactors restart in time to save the ships whose orbits were decaying, the ruins stop killing people, and Elvi's treatment clears the organism from the survivors' eyes. What the Investigator finds in the process is the important part. The civilization that built the gates was not destroyed by a war or a plague but by something that reached in from outside their network and switched them off, and that something is still capable of doing it. Holden brings the warning back with him. On the surface, Murtry makes a last attempt to kill Holden and secure the company's claim by force, and is stopped and taken into custody to be tried for the killings he ordered; Havelock, who has spent the book following orders he disliked, is the one who finally refuses. Lucia Merton faces the consequences of her part in the bombing, and Basia has to live with his. The settlers keep their town and their ore, the company keeps its charter and its scientists, and the two are forced into an uneasy shared occupation of the world. Elvi and Fayez stay on. The gates remain open, and the rush to settle a thousand new worlds continues, now with a warning attached that almost nobody wants to hear.
recaps.in_short: Refugees from Ganymede have squatted on Ilus, the first habitable world reached through the alien gates, and are mining lithium there when Royal Charter Energy arrives holding the United Nations charter for the same planet. Settlers blow up the landing pad, killing the company's governor and shuttle crew, and RCE's security chief Murtry answers with summary executions. James Holden is sent as a mediator, accompanied by an apparition of the dead detective Miller that only he can see and that wants access to the alien ruins. As the two sides escalate toward massacre, the planet itself wakes up: machinery buried for aeons activates, fusion reactors across the system shut down and leave the ships in orbit falling, a tsunami destroys the settlement, and an organism in the water blinds almost everyone. Biologist Elvi Okoye works out a treatment while the survivors shelter together in the ruins. Holden takes the Investigator into the alien network, shuts the planet down, and learns that whatever destroyed the builders is still out there and can reach through the gates. Murtry is arrested, settlers and company are forced to share the world, and the warning goes home with Holden.

recaps.text: Previously: an alien artifact called the protomolecule, released on Eros Station as a corporate experiment, killed more than a million people before the Ceres detective Miller rode the infected station into Venus to keep it from reaching Earth. The protomolecule kept working on Venus, and a later attempt by the industrialist Jules-Pierre Mao to grow protomolecule-human hybrids as weapons was broken on Io by James Holden and the crew of the Rocinante, the Martian marine Bobbie Draper, and the UN official Chrisjen Avasarala. The thing on Venus then lifted off the planet and assembled an enormous ring beyond the orbit of Uranus. When the fleets of Earth, Mars and the Outer Planets Alliance went to investigate it, they were trapped inside the space behind it by defences that had been waiting a very long time; thousands died before Holden reached the alien station at its centre and persuaded it to let them go. An apparition of Miller, an artifact of the protomolecule that only Holden can see, guided him there and has stayed with him since. The ring turned out to be one gate among more than thirteen hundred, each opening onto another star system with habitable worlds behind it. Governments have been arguing over how to control the rush ever since, and the argument has been overtaken by the people already going.

Refugees from the ruin of Ganymede crossed the gates without permission and settled on a habitable world they call Ilus, building a town and mining a rich lithium deposit to pay their way. Earth's answer is Royal Charter Energy, a company holding the United Nations charter for the same planet, arriving with a governor, a security force and a full science team aboard the ship Edward Israel. Told they are squatters on somebody else's property, a group of settlers led by Coop plant explosives on the landing pad, and the blast destroys the incoming shuttle and kills the governor and everyone aboard it. Basia Merton, who lost a son on Ganymede, helped set the charges and immediately regrets it. RCE's security chief, Adolphus Murtry, takes command of the company's response, identifies the men responsible and executes Coop on the spot. The company's biologist, Elvi Okoye, and its security officer Havelock find themselves on an expedition that has become a shooting war before any of the science has begun.

The United Nations sends James Holden and the Rocinante to mediate, on the reasoning that both sides distrust him about equally. Holden has no authority beyond his reputation and a warship in orbit, and neither the settlers nor Murtry intends to be governed by him. He also has a private reason for being there: the apparition of the dead detective Miller travels with him, visible to nobody else, and wants to reach the alien ruins scattered across the planet. Elvi begins cataloguing a biosphere built on chemistry that has nothing to do with Earth's, and finds that almost nothing on the world can eat a human being, which is not the same as the world being safe. Havelock, left aboard the Israel in orbit, watches his employer's position harden and begins recruiting and training the Belter contract workers on the ship into a security force of his own.

The standoff turns lethal. Murtry treats every settler as a combatant, and an exchange at one of the alien ruins leaves people dead on both sides and gives him the excuse to hunt the surviving conspirators. Holden's attempts to arrest and try people through any recognized process are ignored by everyone. Lucia Merton, the settlement's doctor, carries the knowledge of her own part in the bombing, and Basia goes deeper into a resistance he never wanted to join. Naomi goes up to orbit to help the settlers' aging ore ship, the Barbapiccola, which is barely spaceworthy and carries their entire fortune and Basia's daughter. Meanwhile the Investigator leads Holden to the buried machinery under the surface, and something down there begins to respond to being visited.

The planet stops being scenery. Alien structures that have been inert for aeons begin to switch on, one system at a time, without any interest in the humans standing on top of them. Slug-like organisms come out of the ground and kill people who touch them by discharging enormous current. The ruins hum. Elvi, trying to study a catastrophe as it happens, realizes the changes are neither random nor natural but the restart of a machine, and that the machine is the planet. Murtry treats the alien activity as another front in a war he intends to win, and Holden, who has seen what the protomolecule's works do when disturbed, cannot make him hear it. The Investigator becomes more insistent and less coherent, and Holden follows it because there is no one else who knows what any of it means.

The wake-up reaches its peak and the disasters arrive together. A burst from the alien systems shuts down every fusion reactor in the region, leaving the Edward Israel, the Barbapiccola and the Rocinante powerless in decaying orbits with everyone aboard them counting hours. On the ground, enormous structures rise out of the crust and the displacement throws a tsunami across the coast that destroys the settlement of First Landing, killing many and leaving the survivors, settlers and company personnel together, sheltering in the ruins with what they could carry. Naomi comes down with the evacuees and finds she can barely move or breathe in a gravity her body has never known. The war between the two groups becomes irrelevant overnight, though Murtry does not accept that.

Then people start going blind. A microorganism native to the world's water invades human eyes, and within days almost everyone on the surface is sightless, including Holden and most of the settlers, with the company's few remaining medical staff blind alongside them. Elvi, working with failing supplies and her own failing vision, identifies the organism and gambles on an existing drug to kill it. The camp in the ruins survives on rationed water and improvised care, with Basia and Amos hauling supplies and Lucia treating casualties. Murtry, still functional and still armed, uses the chaos to move against the settlers' leadership, and Havelock, ordered to help him, begins to understand exactly what he has been working for.

Elvi's treatment works, and sight starts to come back to the camp. In orbit the ships are still falling, with the Barbapiccola's crew and Felcia aboard and no reactor to lift them, and there are days rather than weeks left. Holden accepts the Investigator's demand and lets it take him down into the alien network beneath the surface, on the theory that the thing that turned the planet on is the only thing that can turn it off. Murtry, who now understands that Holden is the only person able to end the crisis and that ending it on Holden's terms costs the company everything, sets out after him with the last of his loyal security to make certain the machinery is never shut down by anyone but RCE.

Holden reaches the alien machinery and the Investigator does what it came to do. The planet's systems shut down, the reactors restart in time to save the ships in orbit, the ruins go quiet, and the blindness is cured. What the Investigator learns on the way is the larger news: the civilization that built the gates was not destroyed by war or disease but switched off, all at once, by something reaching in from outside their own network, and that something is still there and still capable of it. Murtry makes his final attempt on Holden's life at the alien site and is stopped and taken into custody to face trial for the killings he ordered, with Havelock at last refusing an order. Lucia answers for her part in the bombing and Basia for his. The settlers keep Ilus and their ore, the company keeps its charter and its scientists, and the two are forced into a shared and unhappy occupation of the world. Elvi and Fayez stay to keep studying it. Holden takes the warning home, to a solar system already pouring colony ships through a thousand gates.

characters.description: A sixteen-year-old cyborg and the best mechanic in New Beijing, capital of the Eastern Commonwealth, where she runs a repair booth in the weekly market. A hover accident when she was eleven cost her a hand and a leg, replaced with crude prosthetics, and left her with a retinal display and internal wiring she hides under gloves and boots. She remembers nothing of her life before the surgery. Cyborgs have no legal standing in the Commonwealth, so she is effectively the property of her guardian, who keeps every credit she earns. Practical, blunt and stubbornly competent, she is easier with machines than with people and deeply self-conscious about a body she cannot pass off as ordinary.
characters.name: Linh Cinder

characters.description: The household android belonging to Cinder's guardian, fitted with a faulty personality chip that gives her far more enthusiasm, vanity and opinion than her model was designed for. She helps in the workshop, follows celebrity gossip about the prince, and is the closest thing Cinder has to a friend.
characters.name: Iko

characters.description: The eighteen-year-old crown prince of the Eastern Commonwealth, who comes to Cinder's market booth himself with a malfunctioning royal android he wants repaired quietly. Unpretentious and easy in private, he is under severe strain: his father is dying of the plague, the Lunar queen is pressing him for an alliance, and he expects to inherit the throne far sooner than he wants.
characters.name: Prince Kai

characters.description: An older royal android brought to Cinder's booth by the prince in person for repair. Kai insists the job is urgent, will not say what the android was working on, and asks Cinder to keep the whole matter quiet.
characters.name: Nainsi

characters.description: Cinder's legal guardian and the widow of the man who adopted her. She resents Cinder as an expensive obligation forced on her by a husband who died of the plague within weeks of bringing the girl home, treats her as household property rather than family, and takes everything she earns. She is preoccupied with her daughters' marriage prospects and the family's slipping finances.
characters.name: Linh Adri

characters.description: The younger of Adri's two daughters, fourteen, and the only member of the household who treats Cinder as a sister rather than as a machine. Cheerful and romantic, she is excited about the coming annual ball and helps Cinder scavenge parts in the junkyard.
characters.name: Linh Peony

characters.description: Adri's elder daughter, who shares her mother's contempt for Cinder and is openly embarrassed to be associated with a cyborg.
characters.name: Linh Pearl

characters.description: Kai's father and emperor of the Eastern Commonwealth, respected as a fair and steady ruler. He has contracted letumosis and is dying in quarantine at the palace, leaving his son to manage the Commonwealth's negotiations with Luna.
characters.name: Emperor Rikan

characters.description: The royal advisor, who served Kai's father for years and now steers Kai through his first weeks of rule. Formal and cautious, he is preoccupied above all with the Commonwealth's weak position against Luna.
characters.name: Konn Torin

characters.description: The elderly head of the royal research laboratory, a brisk, evasive scientist leading the search for a cure to letumosis, the plague sweeping Earth. He administers the cyborg draft, in which cyborgs are conscripted as test subjects and do not come back, and takes an unusual and unexplained interest in Cinder once her results come in.
characters.name: Dr. Dmitri Erland

characters.description: The queen of Luna, the settled colony on the moon, whose people can alter what others see and feel. She arrives in New Beijing on the first Lunar state visit in years, pressing for an alliance with the Eastern Commonwealth, and is renowned for a beauty no one at her court is permitted to question. She holds the one thing Earth most needs and intends to be paid for it in crowns.
characters.name: Queen Levana

characters.description: Levana's head thaumaturge, the queen's chief servant and enforcer, who accompanies the Lunar delegation to Earth and handles the work Levana will not do in public.
characters.name: Sybil Mira

characters.description: The heir to the Lunar throne and Levana's niece, believed to have burned to death at the age of three in a fire in the palace nursery. Rumours that the child survived have circulated for years on both worlds, and by the close of the book they have an answer: the missing princess and Linh Cinder are the same person, which makes Cinder the one rival claim Levana cannot ignore.
characters.name: Princess Selene

recaps.ending: Cinder is exposed at the annual ball as both a cyborg and a Lunar, arrested, and sentenced to be handed over to Queen Levana. Cornered, Kai accepts Levana's terms: he will marry her and surrender Cinder in exchange for the letumosis antidote for his people. In her cell, Dr. Erland admits that he is himself a Lunar defector who came to Earth years ago searching for the lost heir, and tells Cinder who she is: Princess Selene, badly burned in the nursery fire Levana ordered, smuggled off the moon at three years old, rebuilt as a cyborg and hidden on Earth ever since. As the only living person with a stronger claim to the Lunar throne, she is the one thing Levana genuinely fears. Erland fits her with a stronger cyborg hand and foot, tells her to break out and find him in Africa, and leaves. Peony is dead of the plague, Iko has been dismantled and survives only as a personality chip, Adri has disowned her, and Kai now knows what she is but not who. The book closes with Cinder alone in the prison, certain of her identity for the first time and choosing to escape rather than be delivered to Luna.
recaps.in_short: In New Beijing, generations after a world war, sixteen-year-old Linh Cinder is a cyborg mechanic owned by an unloving guardian in a society that treats cyborgs as property. When Crown Prince Kai brings her a broken royal android to repair, she is drawn into two crises at once: letumosis, an incurable plague that kills the emperor and her stepsister Peony, and Luna, the moon colony whose queen Levana can bend minds and wants Earth's largest empire through marriage. Conscripted as a plague test subject, Cinder proves immune, and the palace scientist Dr. Erland eventually tells her why: she is Lunar. She goes to the royal ball to warn Kai that Levana means to kill him once she is crowned, and is exposed there as both cyborg and Lunar, then jailed. In prison Erland reveals the rest: Cinder is Princess Selene, the Lunar heir believed dead since childhood and the rightful claimant to Levana's throne. Kai agrees to the marriage to buy the antidote for Earth, and Cinder prepares to break out.

recaps.text: In New Beijing, capital of the Eastern Commonwealth, sixteen-year-old Linh Cinder works as a mechanic in the weekly market. She is a cyborg, rebuilt after a hover accident she cannot remember, and by law the property of her guardian, Linh Adri, who took her in unwillingly after her adoptive father died. Her only real companions are the household android Iko and Adri's younger daughter, Peony. Crown Prince Kai comes to her booth in person with a broken royal android called Nainsi, asking her to repair it quietly. While he is there a man collapses in the market with letumosis, the plague that has killed thousands across Earth and has no cure; the emperor himself is dying of it in the palace. Days later Cinder takes Peony to the city junkyard to scavenge parts for an abandoned car, and Peony collapses with the plague's first mark. Cinder calls the quarantine crews and watches her carried away.

Blaming Cinder for Peony's infection, Adri volunteers her for the cyborg draft, in which cyborgs are conscripted as test subjects for plague research and never return. At the palace laboratory Dr. Dmitri Erland injects her with letumosis and she does not sicken: she is immune, the first case he has ever found. Rather than destroy her he hires her, hoping to trace a cure through her blood, and refuses to explain why he thinks she is different from every other subject. Cinder keeps working on Nainsi and keeps crossing paths with Kai, who is trying to hold off Queen Levana of Luna while his father fails. Emperor Rikan dies of letumosis, and Kai becomes emperor-elect at eighteen with a coronation, a Lunar state visit and an epidemic all bearing down on him at once.

Cinder divides her time between the palace laboratory, where Erland pays her to submit to tests he will not explain, and the market booth that supports Adri's household. Kai, under pressure to accept a marriage alliance with Queen Levana in exchange for Lunar help against the plague, invites Cinder to the annual ball, not knowing she is a cyborg; she cannot accept and cannot explain why. She keeps working on Nainsi and keeps finding that the android's fault is not the interesting thing about her. Peony remains in the quarantine ward, and Cinder visits when she can. The palace braces for Levana's arrival, the first Lunar state visit in years, and Kai has to decide what he is willing to trade for the antidote.

Cinder finishes repairing Nainsi and finds what the android had been doing: the late emperor had secretly ordered her to investigate whether Princess Selene, the Lunar heir believed to have burned to death in the palace nursery at the age of three, might still be alive. Levana arrives in New Beijing with her head thaumaturge Sybil Mira and an entourage whose glamour makes them impossible to see plainly. She offers Kai the plague antidote and an end to Lunar hostility in exchange for marriage and the Commonwealth's crown, and makes clear she will not negotiate. Hiding in the palace, Cinder discovers that she can see through the Lunar glamour and that Levana can neither read nor control her. Dr. Erland gives her the explanation she has been dreading: she is Lunar herself, a fugitive from a people Earth despises, and the gift she has spent her life suppressing is real. He urges her to learn to use it. Levana, having glimpsed her, demands the girl be handed over.

Erland gives Cinder doses of an experimental antidote developed from her own immunity, and she runs them to the quarantine ward for Peony. She arrives too late; Peony dies before the injection can take hold, and Cinder gives the remaining dose to a small boy from the market, who recovers. Before the body is collected she takes Peony's identification chip. Told only that Cinder was at the ward, Adri accuses her of theft and turns on her completely. Cinder now knows she is Lunar, that Levana wants her found, and that Kai is being driven toward a marriage that would hand Earth to Luna.

Adri punishes Cinder by having Iko dismantled and her parts sold, leaving Cinder with nothing but the android's personality chip. Cinder decides she cannot leave the city without warning Kai: Levana intends to marry him, take the Commonwealth, and dispose of him afterwards, and the antidote she is dangling is a lever rather than a gift. She repairs the abandoned orange gravel car in Adri's storage as an escape vehicle, salvages one of Peony's dresses, and resolves to reach Kai at the annual ball, tell him the truth, and be gone before the Lunar delegation can take her.

Cinder arrives at the ball filthy and improvised and gets to Kai. She tells him Levana means to have him killed once she is crowned and begs him to refuse the marriage. Levana confronts them in front of the court and orders Cinder killed as an escaped Lunar fugitive; Kai refuses. Cinder resists the queen's control publicly, and in the struggle to get away her cyborg foot comes loose on the palace stairs, exposing her as both Lunar and cyborg to Kai, the guests and the news cameras. She is arrested and imprisoned to await execution, and Levana renews her demand that the girl be surrendered to Luna.

In her cell Cinder learns Kai has accepted Levana's terms: he will marry her, and Cinder will be handed to Luna, in exchange for the plague antidote for Earth. Dr. Erland visits and admits he is Lunar too, a defector who came to Earth years ago to search for the missing heir. He explains what her scars and her medical records mean: she is Princess Selene, smuggled off Luna as a badly burned three-year-old, rebuilt as a cyborg, hidden for years in Europe and finally placed with the Linh family in New Beijing. Levana ordered the nursery fire, and Cinder is the only person with a legitimate claim to the Lunar throne and the only person Levana truly fears. Erland leaves her an improved cyborg hand and foot, tells her to break out and meet him in Africa, and disappears. The book ends with Cinder alone in the cell, no longer merely a mechanic, deciding to escape.

characters.description: Fifteen, a newly discovered Shadowhunter still living an ordinary Brooklyn life while her mother lies in a coma no doctor can explain. She has begun dating her oldest friend Simon, partly because the alternative is impossible: the boy she actually wants turned out to be her brother. Her one clear gift is for runes, and she has no training worth the name.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Raised as a Shadowhunter and now known to be Valentine's son, which has poisoned his place in the only home he has. He has moved out of the Institute rather than be watched, is sleeping badly, and takes on fights he does not need to. His feelings for Clary have not changed just because he has been told what she is to him.
characters.name: Jace Wayland

characters.description: Clary's oldest friend, now her boyfriend, still an ordinary human in a world that keeps nearly killing him. He is trying to hold on to a normal life of band practice and school while knowing exactly how little he can do if anything goes wrong. Being bitten by vampires last year has left marks he does not talk about.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: The Lightwood daughter, a capable and showy fighter who trains hard and flirts harder. She is protective of Jace in her own way and openly amused by Clary's inexperience, though she is willing to teach her.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: The eldest Lightwood child, careful, dutiful and unhappy. He is keeping two secrets at once: that he is in love with someone he cannot admit to, and that the person is not a Shadowhunter at all. His loyalty to Jace remains absolute even as the Clave's suspicion of Jace grows.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: The Lightwoods' youngest child, nine years old, back from Idris with his mother. He is small, short-sighted, obsessed with stories and manga, and desperate to be taken seriously by the older Shadowhunters who mostly forget he is in the room.
characters.name: Max Lightwood

characters.description: Alec and Isabelle's mother, returned from Idris to run the New York Institute. Formidable and cold under pressure, she was once in Valentine's Circle herself, and the discovery of whose son Jace really is has turned her affection for him into wary suspicion.
characters.name: Maryse Lightwood

characters.description: Clary's mother, still unconscious in a Manhattan hospital after taking a potion to put herself beyond Valentine's reach. She is present in the book mainly as an unanswerable question: nobody knows how to wake her, and much of what she did and why she did it remains hers alone.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Once the Shadowhunter Lucian Graymark, now a werewolf and the leader of a Manhattan pack, and the closest thing Clary has to a guardian while her mother is in hospital. He runs a bookshop, keeps the peace between his pack and the Institute, and lets Jace stay with him when nobody else will.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: A young werewolf of Luke's pack, sharp-tongued and self-possessed, who ran away from a difficult family and was bitten a year or so ago. She meets Jace at a Downworlder bar and dislikes Shadowhunters on principle, having had good reason.
characters.name: Maia Roberts

characters.description: The Clave's Inquisitor, sent from Idris to investigate the New York Institute and the boy Valentine raised. Rigid, grief-hardened and entirely unmoved by anyone's protests, she treats Jace as an enemy agent from the moment she arrives and is willing to imprison a teenager to prove it.
characters.name: Imogen Herondale

characters.description: Clary's father and the leader of the old Circle, at large with the Mortal Cup and no longer bothering to hide. His campaign against the Clave has resumed, and he is collecting the rest of the Mortal Instruments, the objects the angel Raziel left to the first Shadowhunters.
characters.name: Valentine Morgenstern

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, still charging for his services and still watching Alec Lightwood rather more closely than he admits. He is drawn into the Institute's problems repeatedly, and is one of the few people willing to say plainly what the Clave is doing wrong.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: A knight of the Seelie Court, elegant and evasive, who moves between the faerie realm and the city. He is Isabelle's companion for an evening and the escort who brings the Shadowhunters underground when they need an audience with his queen.
characters.name: Meliorn

characters.description: The ruler of the Seelie Court, beautiful, ancient and precise. She grants audiences freely and gives nothing away without a price, and she prefers her prices to be paid in the form of something the payer will regret.
characters.name: The Seelie Queen

characters.description: The leader of the New York vampire clan, boyish in appearance and formally correct in everything he does. He observes the treaties scrupulously, which does not make him an ally, and he arrives at the Institute carrying news nobody wants to hear.
characters.name: Raphael Santiago

recaps.ending: The confrontation ends on Valentine's ship in the East River. He has taken four Downworlder captives, Simon and Maia among them, and completes the ritual that turns the Mortal Sword into a demonic instrument. Jace fights him; the Inquisitor Imogen, who had spent the book trying to destroy Jace, dies taking the blow meant for him, having finally accepted that he is not his father's creature. Simon is drained almost to nothing and revives by drinking Jace's blood, which leaves him a Daylighter, a vampire who can walk in sunlight, something no one has ever heard of. Clary draws an unfamiliar rune on the hull that tears the ship apart, and Valentine escapes into the water with the Cup and the corrupted Sword, leaving two of the three Mortal Instruments in his hands and only the Mirror unaccounted for. The survivors are pulled out of the river by Luke's pack. Maryse's suspicion of Jace is broken and he is welcomed back to the Institute; Clary and Simon have ended their attempt at a relationship, and what happened in the Seelie Court sits unresolved between Clary and Jace, who still believe themselves to be siblings. Jocelyn remains in her coma, and Valentine is stronger than he was.
recaps.in_short: Valentine is at large with the Mortal Cup, and Downworlder children begin turning up dead across the city, drained for a ritual. The Clave sends the Inquisitor Imogen Herondale to New York, convinced that Jace, as Valentine's son, is his father's spy; she imprisons him in the Silent City just as Valentine attacks it, slaughters the Silent Brothers and takes the second Mortal Instrument, the Mortal Sword. Jace escapes and shelters with Luke. Clary and Simon try to be a couple, but an audience with the Seelie Queen forces Clary to kiss Jace in front of him, and Simon walks away; shortly afterwards he is killed and rises as a vampire. The Inquisitor's attempt to trade Jace to Valentine collapses when Valentine shows he does not want him back. Valentine seizes four Downworlders, Simon and Maia among them, to complete a ritual aboard his ship. Clary destroys the ship with a rune of her own making. The Inquisitor dies saving Jace, Valentine escapes with the Cup and the Sword, and Simon, revived on Jace's blood, becomes a vampire who can walk in daylight.

recaps.text: Clary Fray grew up believing she was an ordinary Brooklyn teenager until she saw a demon killed in a nightclub and her mother Jocelyn was abducted the next day. She learned that she is Nephilim, a Shadowhunter, one of the angel-descended hunters who police demons and keep treaties with the Downworlder races, and that her memories had been repeatedly wiped by the warlock Magnus Bane at Jocelyn's request. Her father is Valentine Morgenstern, who once led the Circle in an attempt to purge Downworlders and overthrow the Clave, and who faked his death years ago. Clary recovered the Mortal Cup, the object that creates new Shadowhunters, but the Institute's tutor Hodge betrayed them and handed it, and Jace, to Valentine. At a ruined hospital on the river Valentine revealed that he had raised Jace as his own son under a false name, and that Clary is his daughter, so that Jace and Clary, who had begun to fall in love, believe themselves to be brother and sister. Valentine escaped through a Portal with the Cup. Jocelyn was recovered alive but comatose after drinking a potion to escape him, and lies in a hospital nobody can help her from. Clary's family friend Luke was revealed as a werewolf and a former Shadowhunter, Valentine's old sworn partner, and Clary's best friend Simon, an ordinary human, survived being taken by vampires.

Jace has moved out of the Institute. Maryse Lightwood has come back from Idris with her youngest son Max, and she can no longer look at the boy she helped raise without seeing Valentine's son; the Clave has ordered him watched. Clary is trying to live an ordinary life with her mother still comatose, training a little, and has begun dating Simon largely because the alternative is unthinkable. A faerie child is found murdered and drained of blood, the first of several Downworlder deaths that Downworlders are quick to blame on Shadowhunters. Jace picks a fight at a werewolf bar, where he meets Maia Roberts, a young member of Luke's pack. Then the Clave's Inquisitor, Imogen Herondale, arrives from Idris to conduct her own investigation. She has decided in advance that Jace is his father's agent, and she has him arrested and taken to the cells beneath the Silent City.

While Jace is held in the Bone City, Valentine attacks it. He kills the Silent Brothers, takes the second of the Mortal Instruments, the Mortal Sword, and leaves; Jace survives only because he is already in the cells, and walks out through the wreckage. Because the Clave now assumes he was complicit, he cannot go back to the Institute, and Luke takes him in. The murders of Downworlder children continue, the treaty between the Clave and the Downworlders comes under real strain, and the Inquisitor's grip on the investigation tightens rather than loosens. Clary and Jace keep colliding, unable either to be together or to leave each other alone, and Simon can see it happening.

Needing information about Valentine's plans, Clary, Jace, Simon and Isabelle go down into the Seelie Court. The Queen agrees to help, but sets a price: Clary must be kissed by the person she most desires. Clary tries to make it Simon, and it does not work; she kisses Jace instead, in front of everyone, and Simon watches. He ends their relationship on the way out, hurt but clear-eyed about what he has just seen. Shortly afterwards Simon is killed. Because of the vampire blood already in him from the attack a year earlier, he does not stay dead; he is buried, and Clary calls him out of the grave. He rises as a vampire, and has to work out at once what that means for his mother, his band, his school, and everything else he had been trying to keep.

Simon begins learning what he now is, hiding it from his family and refusing to join Raphael's clan. The Inquisitor decides that Jace's real value is as a bargaining chip and opens negotiations to hand him to Valentine in exchange for the Mortal Instruments, over the Lightwoods' objections. Alec, quietly, is spending more time than he can explain with Magnus Bane. Valentine's collection of Downworlder blood continues, and the pattern of the victims makes clear he is preparing a ritual rather than simply killing. Clary keeps producing runes that are not in any book, and nobody, including her, understands where they come from.

The Inquisitor's bargain collapses. Confronted with the offer of his son, Valentine makes it plain that Jace is worth nothing to him, and the Inquisitor's entire theory falls apart in front of her. Her interference has already weakened the Institute's protections, and demons get in. In the fighting a demon that feeds on fear moves through the building, and Clary invents a rune that makes a person fearless in order to face it. The Inquisitor, who has spent the whole book trying to destroy Jace, ends by defending him. Valentine, meanwhile, has what he needs to begin, and is waiting on the water.

Valentine's ritual requires the blood of one of each of the four Downworlder kinds. He takes captives to complete the set, Simon and Maia among them, and holds them aboard his ship in the East River. Luke's pack, the Lightwoods, Clary and Jace converge on the ship. Clary gets aboard and finds Simon barely alive; Jace goes after his father, and the Inquisitor makes her final choice, dying in Jace's place when Valentine strikes at him. Valentine completes the ritual and the Mortal Sword is turned from a heavenly weapon into a demonic one.

On the sinking ship Simon, drained almost to nothing, drinks Jace's blood and survives; it leaves him a Daylighter, a vampire able to walk in sunlight, which no one has ever heard of before. Clary draws a rune of her own making on the hull and the vessel comes apart around them. Valentine escapes into the water with the Mortal Cup and the corrupted Sword; only the third Instrument, the Mirror, remains unfound, and nobody knows what it is. Luke's pack pulls the survivors out of the river. Maryse's suspicion of Jace is broken and he is taken back into the Institute; Clary and Simon are no longer together; Jocelyn is still in her coma; and what happened in the Seelie Court sits unresolved between Clary and Jace, who continue to believe they are brother and sister.

characters.description: A fifteen-year-old art student living in Brooklyn with her mother. She is small, red-haired, and stubborn, happier drawing than arguing, and has spent her whole life assuming she is entirely ordinary. On a night out at a Manhattan club she watches three armed teenagers kill a boy that nobody else in the room seems able to see, which is the first crack in that assumption.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Clary's best friend since childhood, a bookish, dryly funny teenager who plays in a struggling band with his schoolfriends. He knows nothing of any world beyond the ordinary one and follows Clary into trouble out of pure loyalty. His feelings for her have gone past friendship, which she has not noticed.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: A fair-haired boy of about seventeen, one of the three young hunters Clary sees at the club. Arrogant, quick with an insult, and unnervingly good with a blade, he treats hunting demons as both a duty and a sport. He is genuinely startled that Clary can see him at all, since ordinary people cannot, and that curiosity is what makes him take an interest in her.
characters.name: Jace Wayland

characters.description: A tall, dark-haired girl who hunts alongside Jace and her older brother, armed with a long electrum whip and willing to act as bait to draw a demon out of a crowd. Confident and theatrical, she enjoys the work and has very little patience for ordinary humans.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: Isabelle's older brother, dark-haired, quieter and far more cautious than either of his companions, and fiercely protective of Jace. He distrusts Clary from the moment she appears and resents the disruption she brings into their household.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: Clary's mother, a painter who has raised her alone and told her almost nothing about her own past. Calm on the surface and immovable underneath, she responds to Clary's account of the club by announcing that the two of them are leaving the city at once, and lets slip words that mean nothing at all to her daughter.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Jocelyn's oldest friend, a big, shabby man who runs a second-hand bookshop and has been a steady presence in Clary's life since she was small. When Clary comes to him for help after her mother disappears, he is inexplicably cold to her and sends her away.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: The eccentric woman who occupies the ground-floor apartment of Clary's building, reading fortunes from tarot cards and tea leaves amid a great deal of clutter and a very old set of curtains. She has known Jocelyn for years and clearly knows more about the family upstairs than a neighbour should.
characters.name: Madame Dorothea

characters.description: The tutor at the New York Institute, a greying scholar who trains its young hunters, keeps its library, and is rarely seen without his black bird. Learned and kind in a distracted way, he has not set foot outside the building in many years and shows no sign of wanting to.
characters.name: Hodge Starkweather

characters.description: One of the Silent Brothers, the order of archivists and lorekeepers who guard the Bone City beneath a Manhattan cemetery. His eyes and mouth are sealed with runes and he speaks directly into the minds of those around him. His order can search a person's memory as readily as a book, and their judgement carries weight with the Clave.
characters.name: Brother Jeremiah

characters.description: A Shadowhunter of the previous generation who founded the Circle, a movement that meant to purge the Downworlder races and then turned on its own government. His rebellion was put down years ago and he is believed to have died in a fire; older Shadowhunters still lower their voices when they say his name. He is hunting for the Mortal Cup, the object that can make new Shadowhunters, and he does not much mind who he has to go through to reach it.
characters.name: Valentine Morgenstern

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, a glittering, theatrical figure with cat's eyes who throws enormous parties for the city's Downworlders. Centuries old and expensively bored, he does nothing for free, remembers everything, and takes an immediate interest in the Lightwood brother who cannot look at him directly.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: A vampire of the New York clan who has the face of a boy of fourteen. Courteous, devout, and careful about the treaties that keep his kind and the Shadowhunters from open war, he would rather negotiate a problem away than fight over it.
characters.name: Raphael Santiago

recaps.ending: Hodge Starkweather, once a member of Valentine's Circle and cursed by the Clave never to leave the Institute, betrays the household: he takes the Mortal Cup from Clary and hands Jace over to Valentine in exchange for his freedom. Clary and Luke follow to a derelict building on the river, where Valentine reveals that he raised Jace as his own son under a dead man's name, that Jocelyn is his wife, and that Clary is therefore his daughter. Jace and Clary, who had just begun to fall in love, are told they are brother and sister, and neither of them is given any reason to doubt it. Valentine escapes through a Portal with the Mortal Cup; Clary shatters the mirror behind him so he cannot be followed. Jocelyn is recovered alive but locked in a coma of her own making, and is taken to a hospital where no ordinary doctor can help her. Simon has survived being turned into a rat and nearly drained by vampires; Luke's true nature as a werewolf and former Shadowhunter is out in the open; and Clary is left knowing exactly who her father is, with the Mortal Cup in his hands and her mother beyond waking.
recaps.in_short: Fifteen-year-old Clary Fray watches three teenagers kill a demon in a Manhattan club, an event nobody else can see, and within a day her mother is abducted and her ordinary life is gone. Taken in by the young hunters of the New York Institute, she learns that she is Nephilim, one of the Shadowhunters who police demons and Downworlders, and that her memories have been deliberately blocked for years. Her mother's disappearance is the work of Valentine Morgenstern, a Shadowhunter who once led a rebellion and now wants the Mortal Cup, the object that creates new Shadowhunters. Clary recovers the Cup from a tarot deck her mother painted, learns that her family friend Luke is a werewolf, and discovers a talent for creating runes nobody has seen before. Their tutor Hodge betrays them and delivers the Cup and Jace to Valentine, who reveals that he is father to both Jace and Clary. Valentine escapes with the Cup, and the two are left believing themselves to be siblings.

recaps.text: Clary Fray and her best friend Simon Lewis talk their way into the Pandemonium Club in Manhattan, where Clary watches three armed teenagers her own age corner and kill a blue-haired boy. Simon sees none of it, and when she reports it there is no body. The next day her mother Jocelyn is frightened and insistent that the two of them leave the city immediately, and mentions people and words Clary has never heard. Clary storms out. When she calls home that evening she hears a struggle, and her mother tells her not to come back and to call their old family friend Luke. She goes home anyway to find the apartment wrecked and her mother gone, and is attacked by a demon that she manages to kill with a device one of the club hunters had planted on her. Jace, the fair-haired boy from the club, arrives and takes her, wounded and half-conscious, to a converted church in Manhattan called the Institute.

At the Institute, Clary meets the Lightwoods, Alec and Isabelle, and their tutor Hodge Starkweather, and learns what the world actually contains: Shadowhunters, descended from an angel, who hunt demons with runed weapons under a body of law called the Clave, and Downworlders, the vampires, werewolves, warlocks and faeries with whom they keep an uneasy treaty. Clary is one of the Nephilim herself, and something has been blocking her memories for years. The Institute is attacked, which tells Hodge that Clary matters to somebody. Returning to her ruined apartment with Jace, she meets her downstairs neighbour Madame Dorothea, who knows far more about Jocelyn than a neighbour should. Luke turns Clary away coldly when she goes to him, and she overhears him speaking with two strangers about a man named Valentine and about the Mortal Cup, the object that makes new Shadowhunters, which they are certain Jocelyn has hidden.

Hodge explains the recent history: Valentine Morgenstern founded the Circle, a movement that meant to purge Downworlders and overthrow the Clave, and its uprising was put down years ago; Valentine is believed to have died in a fire, and Jocelyn was his wife. The Silent Brothers take Clary down into the Bone City to search her mind, and find a block placed by the warlock Magnus Bane. Clary and the others crash Magnus's party to demand answers, and he admits Jocelyn paid him to wipe her daughter's memories over and over. During the party Simon is briefly turned into a rat and carried off by vampires.
